changedFields.before:
## Chef's Note

Sear mushrooms in butter until golden rather than boiling them to gray mush. Reserve a cup of seared mushrooms to stir in at the end for textural contrast against the smooth, pureed soup. Dry sherry's acidity and nuttiness bridges earthy shiitakes and rich cream beautifully.

## Directions

1.  **The Sear:** In a large heavy-bottomed pot, melt butter over medium-high heat. Add all mushrooms. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the released liquid has evaporated and the mushrooms are golden, about 10-20 minutes depending on the pot and moisture. Reduce the heat if the butter begins to scorch; browning, not an eight-minute timer, is the endpoint.
2.  **Reserve:** Remove 1 cup of the seared mushrooms and set aside for the garnish.
3.  **Aromatics:** Add shallot to the pot. Sauté for 1 minute until softened, then add garlic and sauté for 30-45 seconds until fragrant. Stir in the thyme, salt, and pepper.
4.  **Simmer:** Pour in the vegetable stock. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes until mushrooms are very tender.
5.  **The Emulsion:** Take the pot off the heat. Use an immersion blender according to its hot-liquid instructions, starting on low with the blade guard submerged; stop the motor before lifting it out. For a countertop blender, use only a container approved for hot liquids, let the soup cool to the manufacturer’s permitted temperature, and follow its fill and venting instructions in small batches. Never blend hot soup in a sealed personal-blender cup. Return the puree to the pot.
6.  **Finish:** Stir in the heavy cream and the **Dry Sherry**. Simmer for 1 more minute.
7.  **Serve:** Ladle into bowls and top with the **Reserved Seared Mushrooms** for texture.
changedFields.after:
## Chef's Note

Cook the sliced mushrooms in butter until their released liquid evaporates and their surfaces turn golden. Set aside a proportional garnish portion before puréeing the rest with stock. The reserved mushrooms contrast with the smooth cream-enriched soup, and the measured dry sherry remains part of the finish.

## Directions

1. **The Sear:** In a large heavy-bottomed pot, melt butter over medium-high heat. Add all mushrooms. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the released liquid has evaporated and the mushrooms are golden, about 10-20 minutes depending on the pot and moisture. Reduce the heat if the butter begins to scorch; browning, not an eight-minute timer, is the endpoint. If the mushrooms crowd the pot too deeply, work in batches, dividing the total measured butter among them and recombining the cooked mushrooms; extra batches add time.

2. **Reserve:** Set aside a proportional portion of the browned mushrooms for the garnish: 1 cup in the original batch with 16 oz cremini and 2/3 cup sliced shiitake. Increase or decrease that garnish portion with the measured mushroom quantity when scaling; keep the rest in the soup pot.

3. **Aromatics:** Add the minced shallot to the remaining mushrooms. Cook about 1 minute as a first check and continue until softened, stirring; add garlic and cook about 30–45 seconds until fragrant. Stir in all the dried thyme and salt and pepper to taste.

4. **Simmer:** Pour in all the vegetable stock. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer about 10 minutes until the mushrooms are very tender.

5. **The Emulsion:** Take the pot off the heat. Use an immersion blender according to its hot-liquid instructions, starting on low with the blade guard submerged; stop the motor before lifting it out. For a countertop blender, use only a container approved for hot liquids, let the soup cool to the manufacturer’s permitted temperature, and follow its fill and venting instructions in small batches. Never blend hot soup in a sealed personal-blender cup. Return the puree to the pot.

6. **Finish:** Stir in all the measured heavy cream and dry sherry. Simmer gently for about 1 more minute, stirring; taste for salt and pepper. Avoid leaving the cream soup at a hard boil.

7. **Serve:** Ladle into bowls and distribute the reserved browned mushrooms among them. Serve promptly.

checkpoints.cue: Free mushroom liquid has evaporated and surfaces are golden; butter is not blackening.
checkpoints.why: Moist mushrooms first release water. Color and moisture matter more than a fixed browning clock.

checkpoints.cue: A mushroom piece is very soft when pressed or bitten.
checkpoints.why: Browning builds flavor, while the stock simmer softens pieces for puréeing.

checkpoints.cue: The machine is off heat, the permitted vessel/load is used, and the purée has no firm pieces.
checkpoints.why: Actual equipment limits govern hot-liquid handling; a smoothness check cannot replace them.

troubleshooting.cause: Released liquid has not evaporated or the pot is overloaded.
troubleshooting.fix: Continue cooking to evaporation and use smaller loads if necessary, dividing the same butter total. Extra batches take longer.

troubleshooting.cause: Heat stayed too high after moisture evaporated.
troubleshooting.fix: Reduce heat sooner next time and watch the butter. Cream or sherry will not remove a burnt flavor.

substitutions.alternative: An immersion blender approved for hot soup
substitutions.effect: Avoids transferring the soup, but still requires that model’s submerged-guard, speed and off-heat handling instructions.

after.timing: Allow 30–40 minutes cooking and approximately 40–50 minutes total: preparation, 10–20 minute mushroom stage, aromatics, stock heating, about 10 minutes simmering and blending/cream finish. Browning, stirring and blending require active attention; the simmer is less active. Extra browning loads, firmer mushrooms or manual-required cooling/reheating add time.
after.storage: Divide leftovers into shallow containers and refrigerate within 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F / 32°C, at 40°F / 4°C or below. Use within 3–4 days. Reheat the portion being served, stirring, to 165°F / 74°C throughout and bring soup to a rolling boil. Stir especially well while reheating the cream soup; it can be less smooth after reheating. Store the mushroom garnish with the soup or in a separate promptly refrigerated shallow container and reheat it for service.
